title: Composed conormal map injective from the coefficient ideal intersection
statement: Let $A\to B\to C$ be a tower of commutative ring homomorphisms. Let $P=A[x_s:s\in\Sigma]\to B$ and $Q=B[y_i:i\in\mathcal I]\to C$ be surjective polynomial presentations [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Let $T=A[y_i,x_s]\to C$ be their composed presentation, $K=\ker(T\to C)$, and $J=\ker(T\to B[y_i])$ for the coefficient map. Suppose $J\cap K^2=JK$. Then the canonical $C$-linear map $C\otimes_B (\ker P/(\ker P)^2)\to K/K^2$, $c\otimes[g]\mapsto c[g]$, induced by the inclusion $A[x_s]\to T$, is injective. The sets of variables may be empty or infinite; no regular-sequence or flatness hypothesis on $B\to C$ is required.

source.place: Tag 07D4, lemma-transitive-lci-at-end, proof: injectivity of the conormal map from IA[x,y] intersect K squared = IK and the final tensor identification. Read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07D4.

proof.text: Let T=(Q.comp P).Ring, I=P.ker, J=ker(Q.ofComp P), and K=(Q.comp P).ker. Mathlib Generators.map_toComp_ker identifies J with the extension of I. The sum-variable polynomial equivalence identifies T with a polynomial algebra over P.Ring, so T is free and hence flat. The multiplication map T tensor I -> J is bijective: injectivity follows by tensoring the ideal subtype and composing with the tensor unit equivalence; its range is the ideal span of the image of I, namely J. This is the private flat_ideal_bijective proof.

For the inclusion J -> K, the map f:J -> K/K² has kernel the preimage of J intersect K². The hypothesis identifies this with JK, the image of K smul top in J. Thus f descends to an injection J/(K smul top) -> K/K². Identify T/K with C by the first isomorphism theorem, then use the quotient tensor equivalence to identify C tensor_T J with J/(K smul top). Checking on c tensor j shows the resulting injection is f.liftBaseChange C. This is the private ideal_injective proof.

Mathlib Extension.cotangentEquiv identifies B tensor_P I with P.Cotangent. Base change to C and cancel B to identify C tensor_B P.Cotangent with C tensor_P I. Cancel T in the other direction and tensor the equivalence of step 1 with C to obtain C tensor_T J. Compose with the injection of step 2. On c tensor Cotangent.mk x, the composite is c smul Cotangent.mk of the polynomial-variable inclusion of x, by contangentEquiv_tmul, cancelBaseChange_tmul and the multiplication formula. It is therefore exactly the displayed conormal map, and is injective.
